title: Payments Desk Reference: Larkspur Credit Cards Minimum Payment, Allocation and Returned Payments
content:
This reference covers payments on the Larkspur Credit Cards: when payments are accepted, how the minimum payment is set, how a payment is applied, and what happens when a payment is returned.

## Accepting payments

Payments are accepted on an account in any status other than applied or declined. Acceptance turns on the status in the account's own system record.

| Account status | Payment accepted? |
|---|---|
| Active | Yes |
| Suspended | Yes |
| Closed | Yes |
| Charged off | Yes |
| Applied | No |
| Declined | No |

## The minimum payment

Each statement's minimum payment is made up as follows:

1. Start with the card's minimum payment percent of the statement balance, plus that cycle's interest and fees. The percentage amount is rounded to the cent.
2. That amount may not be less than the card's lowest minimum payment, unless the full balance is smaller, in which case the full balance is used.
3. Add any amount past due.

The percent and the lowest minimum payment are the figures in the card's product terms. The account record shows the minimum payment due, the payment due date and the amount past due.

The statement's payment due date falls the card's stated number of days after statement closing.

| Situation | Effect on the minimum payment |
|---|---|
| The percentage amount is below the lowest minimum payment, and the balance is larger than the lowest minimum payment | The lowest minimum payment is used |
| The full balance is smaller than the lowest minimum payment | The full balance is used |
| An amount is past due | That amount is added on top |

## Applying a payment

The minimum payment is applied to the lowest-APR balance first. Any amount above the minimum is applied to the highest-APR balance first.

**Hypothetical case.** The balances here are invented. An account carries a purchase balance at one APR and a cash advance balance at a higher APR. A payment larger than the minimum payment is applied as follows:

- the part equal to the minimum payment goes first to the purchase balance, which has the lower APR;
- the part above the minimum goes first to the cash advance balance, which has the higher APR.

## On-time payments and the grace period

Payments by the due date count as on time. A statement balance paid in full by the due date keeps the purchase grace period.

## Returned payments

A returned payment is reversed in full. The amount that had been credited is added back to the amount owed on the card.
